## Historical audit: S0200

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/smoke/smoke_01/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines and events.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, line 1 | The assigned goal was to reconstruct a single 256 × 171 indoor photograph with separate meshes and matched camera and framing. The student’s kitchen interpretation is an inference, not an independently observed description of the reference. |
| Student `model_response` line 3; `execute` line 4 | The program specified multiple objects: walls, cabinet runs and doors, windows, counters, a double sink and faucet. It attempted procedural wood and stone textures, metallic finishes, a camera and three lights. Cabinet pulls had separate mounts and sink openings used subtraction; these are intended connections, not verified geometry. No articulated subject pose was specified. |
| `execution_result` line 5; student request line 6; response line 8; `execute` line 9 | Step 1 failed before rendering: the sink-rim fillet exceeded half its smallest dimension. The student received the traceback and autonomously revised the rim by making a thicker rounded solid, cutting it, then compressing it. |
| `execution_result` line 10; student request line 11; response line 13; `execute` line 14 | Step 2 passed the earlier failure but failed because the scene world was `None`. The student received that traceback and added world creation when absent. These are runner error messages, not teacher feedback. |
| `execution_result` line 15; `select` line 16 | Step 3 reported success, saved a render and scene, and was selected. The log reports 16 render samples despite the program specifying 48; the cause and visual effect are unknown. This establishes technical execution, not geometric or visual fidelity. |
| Student `model_request` line 17; `codex_session` line 18; `model_response` line 19 | The reference and step-3 render were supplied for review with zero executions remaining; the student replied `DONE`. No written comparison or subsequent correction is visible. |

**Outcome and uncertainty.** The run achieved a successful build and render after two execution failures; scene-match correctness is **unknown**, not formally verified. The supplied observations do not show either image’s pixels, so object presence in the reference, material appearance, part connectivity, pose, camera alignment, lighting, occlusion and render quality cannot be independently checked. A name, successful render or `DONE` does not resolve these questions.

No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption is recorded in this student trajectory. The visible exploration consists of the student’s traceback-driven revisions; session records report no tool events (lines 2, 7, 12 and 18).

**Lessons.** Transferably, execution feedback exposed two distinct runtime assumptions before any visual evaluation was possible. Task-specifically, the thicker-then-compressed rim addressed this scene’s fillet constraint, while creating a missing world addressed its Blender environment. Whether the resulting sink geometry or camera and lighting actually match the photograph remains an unresolved hypothesis.
